finding: The n=1 first overtone is ~491x more sensitive to the R4 correction than the n=0 fundamental (driven by dtq_1 = 171.35, ~282x the fundamental's damping coefficient), and the two overtones respond with OPPOSITE sign in the damping: the fundamental decays faster under R4 while the first overtone decays much slower. Overtones probe the near-horizon region where R4 curvature corrections concentrate, so overtone-resolved ringdown is the dominant lever for higher-curvature gravity (cf the active overtone-ringdown literature, e.g. arXiv:2512.22728).
perturbative_caveat: dtq_1 = 171.35 is very large (O(170)); the ParSpec linear-in-gamma expansion is therefore only valid for gamma << 1/170 ~ 6e-3, so the overtone bound is perturbatively DELICATE even as it dominates the constraint. The precise n=1 value should be treated cautiously; the QUALITATIVE result (overtones vastly more sensitive) is robust.
